0|81bd9328ab9f9bf818923b92a64896fd4cf58f2b|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"btrfs: fix repair of compressed extents
Currently the checksum of compressed extents is verified based on the
compressed data and the lower btrfs_bio
is driven by end_bio_extent_readpage on the upper btrfs_bio for the
decompressed data.
This has a bunch of issues
column2: including not being able to properly

column1: communicate the failed mirror up in case that the I/O submission got
preempted
column2: a general loss of if an error was an I/O error or a checksum

column1: verification failure
column2: but most importantly that this design causes

column1: btrfs_clean_io_failure to eventually write back the uncompressed good
data onto the disk sectors that are supposed to contain compressed data.
Fix this by moving the repair to the lower btrfs_bio.  To do so
amount of code has to be reshuffled:
a) the lower btrfs_bio now needs a valid csum pointer.  The easiest way
to achieve that is to pass NULL btrfs_lookup_bio_sums and just use
the btrfs_bio management of csums.  For a compressed_bio that is
split into multiple btrfs_bios this means additional memory
allocations
column2: but the code becomes a lot more regular.

column1: b) checksum verification now runs directly on the lower btrfs_bio instead
of the compressed_bio.  This actually nicely simplifies the end I/O
processing.
c) btrfs_repair_one_sector can't just look up the logical address for
the file offset any more
column2: as there is no corresponding relative

column1: offsets that apply to the file offset and the logic address for
compressed extents.  Instead require that the saved bvec_iter in the
btrfs_bio is filled out for all read bios and use that
removes a fair amount of code.
